title: The Last Ferry
note: Original two-character micro-drama written to stress the native-audio route: 13 spoken lines, two speakers, a range of expressions, storm sound design, an off-screen speaker, a three-line exchange in one shot, scene changes and a night exterior. Publishable: no borrowed characters or voices.
logline: A woman races a storm to reach her dying father; the ferryman who refuses her turns out to have known him for forty years.

A dark ferry silhouette moored to the side, black sea, low clouds. No text, no watermark, no other people.

The older man from the second reference sits behind the counter at RIGHT, looking up from a newspaper. Both faces clearly recognizable and matching their references. No text overlays, no watermark.

shots.visual: A woman hurries along a rain-soaked wooden pier toward the lit window of a small ticket office, suitcase in hand, head down against the wind, rain streaming through the light.
